full.description: This is a biological diagram illustrating the sequential process of apoptosis, or programmed cell death. The diagrams show the morphological changes a normal cell undergoes, including cell shrinkage, chromatin condensation, membrane blebbing, and the formation of apoptotic bodies. Eventually, these apoptotic bodies are engulfed and cleared by phagocytic cells like macrophages. This process ensures the orderly removal of damaged or unnecessary cells without eliciting an inflammatory response.

blind.description: This image is a diagram illustrating microscopic findings associated with bronchial asthma. It shows the characteristic appearance of a Curschmann's spiral and Charcot-Leyden crystals found within a mucus plug. These structures are typical features seen in the airways of patients experiencing asthma exacerbations.
